transcript.text: w/m finally died after 12 yrs, whats the best one to buy under £400? family of 5

For a family of five on a £400 budget, I would look at an 8kg or 9kg machine from brands like Beko, Hoover, or Indesif. These offer good capacity and reliability for the price point, though features may be more basic than premium models. Regarding your old machine dying after 12 years: this is a very long life for a washer. At that age, it is usually due to worn carbon brushes (in brushed motors), a seized pump, or a failed control board. If you are considering repair, check if the motor has carbon brushes; replacing them is cheap and easy. However, given the age, replacement is often more cost-effective long-term. If you'd like specific model recommendations within your budget, let me know your preferred brand or any must-have features (e.g., steam care, quiet spin).
it stopped mid-cycle 2 days ago with water still in the drum, won't drain or spin, just hums. would fix it if its cheap tho

That humming sound with water still in the drum usually means the machine is trying to pump but can't because something is blocking it or the pump has failed. Since you want a cheap fix, the most likely culprit is a blockage in the drain filter (often coins, buttons, or lint) or an object stuck in the pump itself. This is often a free repair if caught early. Please switch off and unplug the machine first for safety, then open the small access panel at the bottom front to check the filter—tell me what you find inside and whether the little fan blades behind it spin freely by hand.
didn't know there was a filter tbh. water's still in the drum so will it flood when I open it? its a Hotpoint WMBF944P

Don't worry about flooding. There will be a small amount of water in the bottom tray behind that panel, but if you put a shallow container (like a baking tray) or some thick towels underneath before opening it, any water that escapes will just drip into that instead of onto your floor. To keep things tidy, unscrew the filter very slowly and let the water drain out gradually into your container. Once it has stopped trickling, pull the filter out fully to check for blockages like coins or lint.
ok will unplug it first. theres still a full drum of water in there tho, is that going to all come out the filter? will try it now

No, only the small amount of water sitting in the bottom sump (behind that panel) will come out—the rest stays safely in the drum until the pump moves it. Since you are about to open it, please unscrew the filter slowly into your container as planned.
ok, tray and towels ready. will open it slowly now and tell you what I find

Take your time with it. Once you have the filter out, please check two things: first, look for any blockages like coins or debris that might be stopping the water from leaving; second, shine a light into the hole and gently turn the small plastic impeller (the fan blades) with your finger to see if it spins freely or feels jammed. Let me know exactly what you find there.
got the panel open and the water's out into the tray, but I'm not sure what I'm looking at tbh. can't really tell if anything's stuck or if the fan thing spins. what should I look for?
If they are jammed by an object, that is likely the cause. If they spin freely but nothing was found, it suggests the pump motor itself may have failed.
so what am I looking for exactly? cant tell if anything's stuck or if the fan spins. kinda busy, need a quick answer

I understand you're busy, so here's exactly what to look for: inside the hole where the filter was, you should see a small plastic fan-like wheel (the impeller). Try turning it gently with your finger. If it spins freely but nothing was in the filter, the pump motor has likely failed and needs replacing.
